analysis.title: International Market Intelligence Morning Briefing
key_insights: Global risk-on with Tech leading gains as AI optimism returns, with TSMC and CRWV helping the bounce.

US equities lagged global peers after a hot US CPI and hawkish Fed comments drove a sharp UST selloff. The US 2Y had its biggest move since Apr-25 and the selloff spilled into global rates. Markets price a possible 50bps Fed hike in Dec.

US inflation concerns returned while energy prices fell. Brent broke below $90 after Trump pulled back strike threats, and US-led RU/UA peace talks resume. JPM's commodities desk sees Brent fair value at $80-$85.

Oil and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz (SOH) are normalizing but strikes continue. TTF prices in Europe should stay elevated on colder weather and a renewables shortfall that is accelerating storage withdrawals.
The improving geopolitical narrative is a positive for Europe and international equities. India stands out, with its rally extending on foreign net buying.
Broadening supports the EM trade through lower oil prices, declining bond yields and a weaker or stable dollar. The thematic focus should remain on non-AI too.
After the October neocloud meltdown, CRWV eased funding anxieties by disclosing it will rely more on customer prepayments than additional borrowing.
On who is buying hyperscaler bonds, JPM credit strategists say asset managers have led buying so far, while insurers remain underweight with scope to add as price creates capacity.
In US electricals, Research turned more cautious on AI-linked names but expects a sharp bounce given the speed of the selloff. Sustaining it requires improving customer ROI on AI spend.
After the midterms, GPU rental prices are the key indicator to watch as a measure of compute scarcity.

Japan flows: Japanese investors net bought ¥0.5tn of foreign bonds in August, led by pension funds (¥0.8tn). BoP data through September shows no EUR bond selling. JPM sees no GPIF allocation shift signal in MoF October data.

FX margin positioning: short JPY exposure keeps building in JPY crosses, while short JPY vs USD positions were trimmed. Japanese retail net bought ¥1tn of foreign equities for a fourth month in October, and JPM expects that appetite to stay intact.

China trade: exports eased from September's high but stayed strong, imports rose on energy and tech supply chain needs, and the trade surplus narrowed. The full-year total is on track to exceed last year's.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. Its regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus Europe. It sees the US as overheating and Europe as recovering from stagflation.
Broadening can return more clearly in the US than in Europe. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EGB spread stability is needed for conviction.

Prime Brokerage note: multi-strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid. After 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile, as on Oct. 27, alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

Hedge fund net leverage fell about 4% in the past week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low. Semis were the most net-sold US theme, and global momentum exposure is near three-year lows.
In Europe, short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022. North America and Japan saw net selling, while EMEA and China/HK saw net buying.

Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. APAC momentum exposure fell quickly from more extreme levels.
Semis were the most net-sold US theme and positioning is back near early-2026 levels. Software flows were neutral and positioning continues to recover.

European short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.
